additional_concerns: Footnote 5 repeats demonstration without an express request condition. The executable preserves the question's stipulated request-conditioned reading; it does not resolve the rival reading that demonstration is independently required by the footnote. The reach of the high-confidence qualification also remains unresolved.

TRUE_IS_SATISFIED denotes satisfaction of the request condition only. Neither Boolean result establishes confirmation, demonstration, SFC satisfaction, adequate supervision, operational soundness or accurate ownership records.
Paragraphs 15 and 16 impose distinct request-conditioned audit/verification and legal-opinion duties. A paragraph 14 demonstration request does not automatically activate either.

The ownership-record and compatibility provision, Code 6.8 register requirements, valuation-specific Code 6.11C supervision standard, and intermediary provisions 13 and 17–18 do not supply additional conditions for this narrowly typed trigger. Their applicability cannot be assumed to establish provider fulfillment.

Full paragraphs 10–13 and the referenced Appendix factors are not supplied. They would be needed to assess the complete substantive demonstration or fulfillment standard, but their absence does not prevent assessment of this stipulated trigger.

authority.rationale: The supplied paragraph 10 and footnote 1 establish continuing responsibility directly; no additional external authority is needed for this claim.

executable_correspondence.rationale: Continuing responsibility is outside the demonstration-activation question. Its absence from the trigger formula is not an omission relative to that question.

evidence.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

question_relation.rationale: This continuing underlying duty does not determine whether the SFC has made an applicable demonstration request. It persists regardless of the trigger result.

evidence.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

source_support.rationale: Paragraph 10 expressly assigns ultimate responsibility for management and operational soundness; footnote 1 reinforces retention of full responsibility despite outsourcing. This establishes responsibility, not a complete test of fulfillment.

authority.rationale: The supplied paragraph 14 and footnote 5 suffice to assess the expressly stipulated reading. No additional external dependency is needed for that conditional assessment.

executable_correspondence.rationale: Within provider_in_scope, the result is demonstration_requested, exactly testing activation under the stipulated reading. The supplied fact definitions limit the request to this provider, arrangement and paragraph 14 duty. Performance and SFC acceptance are outside this result.

followup_questions: Does footnote 5 specify only minimum demonstration content, or independently require demonstration without an SFC request?
Does the high-confidence qualification apply only to absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities and security flaws, or also to compliance with paragraphs 10–13?

evidence.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

question_relation.rationale: The claim supplies the very request condition tested by the typed question, which expressly adopts the reading that footnote 5 specifies content without removing that condition.

evidence.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

source_support.rationale: Paragraph 14 expressly supports demonstration upon request of all three specified matters to SFC satisfaction. Footnote 5 adds minimum content. The positive duty upon request is supported under either reading; the stronger inference that no demonstration duty exists without a request remains interpretive.
